facts.text: On this day in 1918, the Armistice ending WWI took effect at the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month — a time chosen deliberately for its symmetry, not military necessity.
On this day in 1965, Rhodesia declared independence from Britain. It was the first unilateral such declaration by a British colony since 1776.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka, Bangladesh than in the entire United States west of the Mississippi River.
The Vatican has a higher crime rate per capita than any country on Earth — roughly 1.5 crimes per resident annually — almost entirely due to pickpocketing among its millions of daily visitors.
Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined, holding roughly 60% of the world's fresh lake water within its borders.
On this day in 1918, the Armistice ending WWI was signed — within hours, commodity markets reopened and cotton futures surged 10% as traders priced in the end of wartime price controls.
On Nov 11, 1929, two weeks after the great crash, the Dow posted its single largest one-day gain to that point — a 9.5% rally that fooled thousands into believing the panic was over.
The NYSE's famous "closing bell" was originally a gong, and for decades traders simply ignored it — the exchange didn't gain real authority to halt floor trading until 1871.
Saudi Aramco briefly hit $2 trillion in market cap in 2019, making it worth more than the entire GDP of Italy, Canada, or South Korea — each of which has over 35 million people.
The U.S. penny costs 3.7 cents to produce. The government loses money on every one it mints — a centuries-old fiscal absurdity kept alive almost entirely by the zinc lobby.
On this day in 1572, Tycho Brahe observed a supernova so bright it was visible in daylight — proving the heavens were not, as Aristotle insisted, eternal and unchanging.
On November 11, 1930, Einstein endorsed a refrigerator with no moving parts. It worked via thermodynamics alone and is now being revived to cool vaccines off-grid.
Your brain generates roughly 23 watts of heat — enough to dimly light an LED bulb — entirely as a byproduct of thinking.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its matter would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.
Tardigrades can survive the vacuum of open space. In 2007, exposed specimens returned alive — the only animal confirmed to endure unshielded spaceflight.

On this day in 1918, the WWI armistice took effect at the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month — a time chosen purely for symbolic tidiness, costing roughly 11,000 casualties on the final morning alone.
Oxford University was teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. Oxford dates to 1096; Tenochtitlan wasn't founded until 1325.
On this day in 1620, the Mayflower Compact was signed — the same week Galileo was corresponding with colleagues about Jupiter's moons, two worlds utterly unaware of each other.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She died in 30 BC; the pyramid was finished around 2560 BC.
The fax machine was patented in 1843, before the American Civil War. Alexander Bain's device could transmit images over wire while most people still received news by horseback.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in 2012, it spread so fast it feels ancient.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of used bookshops. Also Koenig's invention — proof that naming a feeling summons the proof it was always real.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home you cannot return to, or never had. Untranslatable, because no other language decided this specific ache deserved its own word.
On this day in 1918, the Armistice ending WWI took effect at 11 a.m. The word 'armistice' comes from Latin arma (arms) + stitium (stoppage) — a ceasing of weapons, built into a single breath.
Remembrance Sunday falls near today every year, and the word 'poppy' traces to Old English popæg — a plant whose red made it, centuries later, the perfect symbol for blood returned to field.
On Nov 11, 2021, Ethereum's EIP-1559 had already burned over 1 million ETH in its first three months — permanently removing more supply than many altcoins ever minted.
On Nov 11, 2022, FTX filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, with Sam Bankman-Fried resigning the same day — $8B in customer funds were simply gone.
Bitcoin's smallest unit, the satoshi, wasn't named in Satoshi Nakamoto's whitepaper. The term was coined by forum users in 2010 and adopted retroactively.
The DAO hack of 2016 didn't exploit a bug in Ethereum — it executed the contract exactly as written. The code worked; the design was the flaw.
Ethereum's genesis block contains a hidden message: the Times headline 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — the same text Satoshi embedded in Bitcoin's block zero.

On this date in 1966, ELIZA—the first chatbot to pass casual conversation for human—was described in a paper by Joseph Weizenbaum. Its creator was so disturbed by how readily people anthropomorphized it that he became an AI critic.

On this date in 2022, Meta released Galactica, a large language model trained on scientific text. It was pulled offline after 72 hours when researchers demonstrated it confidently fabricated citations, dosages, and historical facts.
GPT-4 was trained on roughly 25,000 A100 GPUs for an estimated 90–100 days. The electricity cost alone is pegged around $63 million—before accounting for hardware depreciation or engineering time.

AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins in 2022, more than all experimental structures accumulated by biology since X-ray crystallography began in the 1950s. The entire database was released free.

Reinforcement learning from human feedback uses surprisingly few labels: InstructGPT's alignment was shaped by around 40 contractors comparing model outputs. That small group's preferences now influence billions of daily interactions.
